_comment: swarm-court lane cards. Edit freely: qa.py reads this file on every run. 'prefix' is used for finding IDs (e.g. RC-001); 'aliases' are accepted by --lanes/--skip; checklist items are numbered 1..N in hunter briefs and in the coverage matrix.

lanes.name: Functional
lanes.mission: Prove the feature does what the business rules say, and fails correctly when it shouldn't succeed.
checklist: Happy path with valid inputs
Invalid inputs (missing fields, wrong types, malformed values)
Boundary values (min, max, zero, negative, empty strings)
Optional fields (omitted, explicitly null, empty, populated)
Business rules (permissions, status transitions, limits, dependencies)
Duplicate actions (repeated submit, double-click, retry, refresh)
CRUD lifecycle (create, read, update, delete, restore)
Invalid state transitions
Error responses (status code, message, validation structure)
Regressions in neighbouring functionality
techniques: Map every route to its FormRequest/validator and compare the rules with the business rules in scope.md
Walk each status/state machine and try every transition that is NOT allowed
Feature tests that assert status code, JSON structure and the resulting DB state (assertDatabaseHas/Missing)
Probe null vs missing vs empty for every optional field (Laravel: 'sometimes', 'nullable', 'present', 'filled')
Re-run neighbouring feature tests that share models or services with the changed code
lanes.evidence_standard: Exact request payload + expected vs actual response/state.

lanes.name: Race conditions
lanes.mission: Find any place two requests, workers, or callbacks touching the same resource can corrupt state.
checklist: Two users update the same record -> no silent lost update
Two requests create the same unique entity -> only one succeeds or idempotent handling
Two workers process the same job -> no duplicate side effects
Concurrent stock or balance deductions -> no overselling or negative balance
Update and delete simultaneously -> no inconsistent or resurrected data
Two payment callbacks together -> applied exactly once
Job retries while the original still runs -> no duplicate processing or conflicting writes
Multiple requests change status -> only valid transitions commit
techniques: Look for read-check-write patterns without locks
Missing lockForUpdate() / sharedLock()
Non-atomic increment/decrement (read then save instead of a single UPDATE with a WHERE guard)
Uniqueness enforced only by validation rather than a DB unique index
Missing idempotency keys on payments and external API calls
Transactions that don't cover the whole invariant
firstOrCreate/updateOrCreate without a unique index
Jobs lacking ShouldBeUnique / WithoutOverlapping
Cache-based locks without expiry
Optimistic-locking (version) columns missing

HARD RULE: a single-threaded test that calls the same endpoint twice in sequence does NOT reproduce a race. Reproduction tests must use real parallelism: separate OS processes or separate DB connections (e.g. spawn N `php artisan` / `php -r` child processes, or Laravel's Concurrency facade / Process::pool, released together by a barrier such as a file lock or a DB advisory lock). If real parallelism is impossible in the sandbox, the finding can be at most LIKELY, never CONFIRMED.
lanes.evidence_standard: The unguarded read-modify-write lines (file:line) + a parallel test and the final inconsistent state (e.g. quantity = -1, two orders, two payments).
lanes.skip_when: Only static content or read-only endpoints with no shared mutable state.

lanes.name: Data integrity
lanes.mission: Find ways data ends up wrong, orphaned, partial, or lossy.
checklist: Record missing, deleted or inaccessible
Related record missing or deleted
Nullable foreign keys and optional relationships
Empty and very large result sets
Duplicate records and conflicting unique keys
Invalid dates, leap days, month boundaries, timezone conversions (DST, UTC vs app timezone)
Numeric precision, rounding, overflow, decimal boundaries (floats for money!)
Unicode, emoji, whitespace-only, very long strings (column length truncation)
Unexpected or stale enum/status values
Partial failure in a multi-step operation
Transaction rollback leaving partial changes (emails, events, queue dispatches that fire before commit; use afterCommit)
Soft-deleted records in queries and uniqueness checks
Bulk operations with mixed valid and invalid rows
techniques: Compare model casts and migration column types (decimal vs float, string length vs validation max)
Find side effects (mail, events, dispatch, HTTP calls) inside DB::transaction that are not afterCommit
Check every relationship access for null-safety when the related row is deleted or soft-deleted
Look for unique checks that ignore deleted_at, and Rule::unique without ->ignore() on update
Probe Carbon parsing/formatting with the app timezone vs UTC and DST transition dates
lanes.evidence_standard: The exact input or sequence + the resulting wrong/orphaned/partial row(s) (table, column, value), with file:line of the code that allowed it.

lanes.name: Authorization & security
lanes.mission: Find any way to do or see something you shouldn't.
checklist: Unauthenticated -> 401
Authenticated without permission -> 403
Changing an ID to reach another tenant's/user's record (IDOR)

Tenant isolation on EVERY read, write, export, background job and relationship traversal (withoutGlobalScopes, raw queries, DB::table, jobs losing tenant context, cache keys without tenant, signed URLs, exports)
Request validation rejects unexpected fields
Mass assignment ($guarded = [], $request->all() into create/update)
API resource/schema leaks of sensitive fields
Pagination/filter/sort/search injection
Rate limiting on expensive or sensitive endpoints (login, password reset, export, search)
Sensitive data in logs and error messages
CORS, CSRF, token/session expiry
SQL injection (raw/whereRaw/orderBy with user input)
Stored and reflected XSS
techniques: For every route: list middleware, the policy/gate call ($this->authorize, Gate::allows, can: middleware) and what happens when it is missing
Route-model binding without scoping (->scopeBindings(), where user_id = auth id)
Grep for withoutGlobalScope(s), DB::table, DB::raw, whereRaw, orderByRaw, selectRaw on code paths in scope
Compare $fillable/$guarded with what the request actually passes; check $hidden and API Resources for leaked fields
Act as user A and request user B's resources by ID in a feature test (actingAs)
Safety: payloads are only used against the local test app. No attack tooling, no scanning of external hosts.
lanes.evidence_standard: The request made as which user/tenant, the resource it reached, and the missing check (file:line). A failing actingAs() test is the gold standard.
lanes.skip_when: Never skipped for anything reachable by a user, API client, or job.

lanes.name: Database
lanes.mission: Make the database the last line of defence and make sure it performs.
checklist: Foreign key and unique constraints exist and match business rules
Commit on success and rollback on failure
Concurrent writes preserve invariants
Indexes on all filter/sort/join columns used by this feature
No N+1 on list and detail endpoints (missing eager loading, preventLazyLoading behaviour)
Soft-delete / restore / cascade correctness
Migration works on a POPULATED database (default values for new NOT NULL columns, long-running locks on big tables)
Rollback or forward-recovery path verified
Connection loss and deadlock retry handled safely (and not retried when the operation is non-idempotent)
techniques: Read every migration in scope; list constraints and indexes; compare with the queries the code issues
Count queries per request with DB::listen / DB::enableQueryLog on a handful of rows
EXPLAIN the feature's queries on a small seeded dataset
Check down() methods and whether a migration can run twice or on existing rows
Look for DB::transaction(..., attempts) wrapping non-idempotent side effects
lanes.evidence_standard: Migration/query file:line + the constraint or index that is missing (or the query count / EXPLAIN output) and the concrete data that violates or slows it.

lanes.name: Queue, cache & external services
checklist: Job succeeds normally
Retries after transient failure
Permanent failure lands in failed_jobs (or equivalent)
Retried jobs don't duplicate DB changes or external side effects (emails, charges, webhooks)
Worker timeout < retry_after consistency
Job payloads serialise models safely (deleted models, SerializesModels)
Redis unavailable -> safe degradation or clear failure
Cache invalidation after relevant writes
Stale cache can't expose unauthorised or outdated data
External API timeout, 429, malformed response, outage handled with backoff and circuit breaking
Webhook signature validated and duplicate delivery is safe
Out-of-order webhook delivery
Scheduled jobs don't overlap or silently skip work (withoutOverlapping, onOneServer)
techniques: Read config/queue.php retry_after vs job $timeout / worker --timeout
List every side effect inside handle() and ask what happens if handle() runs twice
Use Queue::fake / Bus::fake / Http::fake / Event::fake / Mail::fake; never call real external services
Check $tries, $backoff, failed() and $deleteWhenMissingModels on each job
For webhooks: signature check before any work, unique provider event id stored, status transitions guarded
lanes.evidence_standard: The job/listener/webhook file:line + the replay/retry/outage sequence and the duplicated or lost side effect, using fakes (no real external calls).
lanes.skip_when: No jobs, listeners, cache, scheduler, webhooks or external HTTP calls in scope.

lanes.name: Performance & latency
lanes.mission: Measure latency on the local app and find what falls over at 10x: endpoints whose p95 breaks the budget, cost that grows faster than the data, too many queries, memory blow-ups, and slow pages.
checklist: Latency of every endpoint in scope: p50/p95/p99 measured locally with bench.py against the budget in scope.md (rubric defaults if none)
Scaling: the same endpoint/job at two data sizes (e.g. 1k vs 10k rows); growth must be flat or sublinear for paginated reads
Query count per request (DB::listen / query log): N+1, queries inside loops, missing eager loading
Query plans: EXPLAIN on filter/sort/join columns; unbounded queries and accidental full-table scans
Memory in exports/imports/bulk operations (get() vs chunk/cursor/lazy): peak memory at two data sizes
Pagination, chunking and streaming for anything that can return many rows
Expensive reports and integrations run async (queue) instead of inside the request
Lock contention and long transactions on hot rows/tables
Frontend cost: requests per page load, polling frequency, payload size, re-render on every poll, bundle size if a build exists
Behaviour when DB, Redis or queue capacity is saturated (timeouts, retries, backpressure) - by reasoning, never by generating load
techniques: Serve the app (or a minimal reproduction) on 127.0.0.1 and time it ONLY with bench.py (http/cmd/compare); it refuses non-local targets and caps every run
Seed a TEST SQLite/MySQL DB at two sizes and use `bench.py compare --size-small N --size-large 10N`: superlinear growth is the strongest evidence
Count queries with DB::listen / DB::enableQueryLog (or the stack's equivalent) and save the output under .swarm-court/<run>/tests/
EXPLAIN the feature's queries on the seeded data; save the plans
memory_get_peak_usage() (or the stack's equivalent) around jobs/exports at two sizes
Static analysis first: loops that query, ->get()/->all() without limits, missing pagination, work that should be queued
Safety: bench.py measurements only, never heavy load or stress tests, never against anything but localhost
lanes.evidence_standard: file:line of the slow/unbounded code + a saved measurement under .swarm-court/<run>/tests/ (bench.py JSON, query counts, EXPLAIN, peak memory), ideally at two data sizes showing the growth, compared with the budget.
lanes.skip_when: Trivial changes (copy, config, single-row reads) unless latency was explicitly requested.

lanes.name: Frontend logic & security
lanes.mission: Find bugs in the code that runs in the browser: broken API contracts, stale or racing requests, client-only security, XSS sinks, leaked timers, and state that drifts from the server.
checklist: API contract: every field a component reads exists in the API/Resource/Inertia-prop response with the same name, type, nullability and pagination shape
Client-side validation matches the server rules (required, formats, min/max, date order); server 422 errors are mapped to the right fields
Stale or out-of-order responses: a slower earlier request cannot overwrite a newer one (search, filters, pagination, tab switches); requests are aborted or sequenced
Repeated actions: submit buttons disabled or requests de-duplicated while pending (double click, Enter + click, retry)
Failed requests are surfaced, not swallowed (missing catch, unhandled promise, generic message hiding the real error, error boundary)
Client-only security: actions hidden in the UI but allowed by the API, route guards without server checks, permissions or IDs taken from client state
Secrets and data leaks: tokens or keys in the JS bundle, auth tokens in localStorage, Inertia shared props or page props exposing fields the user must not see
XSS sinks: v-html, {!! !!}, x-html, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, user content in href/src (javascript:), unescaped Livewire/Alpine output
Livewire/Alpine: public properties and action parameters are client-controlled (#[Locked], authorization inside actions, wire:model on sensitive fields)
Polling, websockets, intervals and listeners stop on unmount and on terminal states; no duplicate pollers after re-render or navigation
Optimistic updates roll back on failure; local state matches the server after an error, refresh or reconnect
Routing and deep links: refresh, back button, direct URL and query-string state behave; 403/404/419 (CSRF/session expired) are handled
Dates, numbers and money: timezone/locale formatting, no float maths on money, date inputs sent in the format the server expects
Downloads and uploads: auth on file requests, filenames, blob/object-URL cleanup, size/type limits enforced server-side too
techniques: List every HTTP call (axios/fetch/useFetch/router.get/post, Inertia router, wire: actions) and map it to its backend route; then diff the fields the template reads against what the controller/API Resource actually returns
Grep for XSS sinks: v-html, x-html, {!!, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, :href bound to user data
Grep for setInterval/setTimeout/addEventListener/Echo.listen and check the matching cleanup (onUnmounted/onBeforeUnmount/useEffect return/Alpine destroy)
For every async handler: is there a catch? Is the pending flag reset in finally? Can two calls interleave?

Component tests with Vitest/Jest + Testing Library or @vue/test-utils, mocking HTTP (vi.fn/msw), when node_modules is installed. E2E (Playwright/Cypress) only if already installed and only against localhost

Without node_modules: deterministic static proof (e.g. the API Resource has no download_url, so the template reads undefined), or a minimal plain-node script under .swarm-court/<run>/tests/ reproducing the logic (e.g. two promises resolving out of order)
Security bugs found here (XSS, client-only authorization, leaked data) use category authz so the release gate treats them as security; logic/state bugs use category frontend
Never install dependencies and never start servers on a public interface
lanes.evidence_standard: Component file:line + the user action sequence + what the user sees vs what they should see. For contract bugs, also the backend file:line that proves the field/shape is missing. CONFIRMED needs a component/E2E test run or a deterministic static proof.
lanes.skip_when: No browser code in scope (no JS/TS/Vue/React/Svelte files, no Blade/Livewire/Inertia views).

lanes.name: UI / UX
lanes.mission: Find where the interface lies to, loses, or blocks the user.
checklist: Loading, empty, success and error states
Form errors shown beside the relevant field
Double submission prevented
Refresh and back-navigation don't corrupt state
Session expiry handled
Responsive layout
Accessibility (labels, focus, contrast, keyboard)
Date/time display respects configured timezone
Accurate status while background processing is pending
techniques: Read Blade/Livewire/Inertia/Vue/React components for every state branch
Check submit buttons for disabled/pending handling and server-side idempotency
Check form error bag binding per field
Check that timestamps are formatted in the user's/app timezone
Check form controls for associated labels, buttons for accessible names, icon-only buttons for aria-label, and focus management after dialogs/navigation
lanes.evidence_standard: Component file:line + the user action sequence + what the user sees vs what they should see.
lanes.skip_when: No UI (views, components, pages) in scope.

lanes.name: Chaos & ops
lanes.mission: Find what breaks on deploy, under failure, or at 3am when nobody is watching.
checklist: Environment variables and secrets present and correct
Production debug off
Migrations and deploy order safe
Queue workers restart on release (queue:restart) and use the right release
Logs carry correlation IDs without sensitive data
Monitoring and alerts for failures, latency, queue backlog
Backup restore tested
Rollback and incident recovery documented
techniques: Read config/*.php, .env.example, deploy scripts, CI config, Dockerfiles, Procfile/supervisor configs
Check that new env keys have config() defaults and are in .env.example (never print real .env values)
Check deploy order: migrate before code that needs new columns; code tolerant of old schema during rollout
Note: mostly static/config review. Never run destructive commands.
lanes.evidence_standard: Config/deploy file:line + the deploy or failure sequence and its consequence.
lanes.skip_when: Pure refactor with no config, deploy, migration or infrastructure impact.

lanes.name: Adversary
lanes.mission: Ignore the checklist and break the feature like a hostile or clumsy real user.
checklist: Replay requests
Reorder steps
Stale tabs and expired tokens
Call the API directly, skipping the UI
Absurd sizes (huge payloads, huge numbers, huge lists)
Switch accounts mid-flow
Double-click everything
Abuse optional parameters
Chain two features together in ways nobody designed
techniques: Start from every public entry point (routes, webhooks, signed URLs, commands) and ask what the UI was protecting
Combine this feature with neighbouring ones (cancel then pay, refund then ship, delete then restore)
Treat every client-supplied value (prices, totals, IDs, flags) as attacker-controlled
lanes.evidence_standard: The exact request sequence a real user or attacker would send + the resulting state.
